questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Choose the verb form that agrees with a singular subject
questions.stem: The boy ____ to school every day.
questions.stepByStepExplanation: The subject ‘The boy’ is singular. In the simple present, singular third-person subjects take the -s form of the verb: goes.
questions.commonMisconception: Using the base form ‘go’ because it sounds natural in casual speech, especially in some Nigerian English varieties.
questions.aiTutorContext: Emphasize singular subject → verb + s in present simple. Contrast with plural: The boys go.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Apply concord rules with collective nouns used as a unit
questions.stem: The committee ____ decided on a new date.
questions.stepByStepExplanation: When a collective noun (committee) acts as a single unit making one decision, it takes a singular verb: has decided.
questions.commonMisconception: Always treating collective nouns as plural (have) regardless of whether the group acts as one unit or as individuals.
questions.aiTutorContext: Explain unit vs individuals: The committee has decided (one decision) vs The committee have disagreed among themselves (individuals).

questions.subject: English Language
questions.stem: Neither the teacher nor the students ____ present.
questions.stepByStepExplanation: With neither…nor, the verb often agrees with the nearer subject. Here ‘students’ is plural and nearer the verb, so were is correct.
questions.commonMisconception: Always using a singular verb after neither, ignoring the nearer-subject rule.
questions.aiTutorContext: Teach the proximity rule with clear examples: Neither the students nor the teacher was present (teacher nearer → singular).

questions.subject: English Language
questions.learningObjective: Use singular verbs with indefinite pronouns like everyone
questions.stem: Everyone ____ expected to submit the form today.
questions.stepByStepExplanation: Indefinite pronouns such as everyone, somebody, each are grammatically singular and take singular verbs: is expected.
questions.commonMisconception: Matching the verb to the idea of many people (are) instead of the grammatical singularity of everyone.
questions.aiTutorContext: List common singular indefinites: everyone, somebody, nobody, each, either. Drill short sentences.
